subtopic: Mixed precision / Master weights / Accumulation dtype
learningObjective: Explain the master-weight pattern in mixed-precision DNN training and the roles of the various dtypes.
stem: Standard mixed-precision (FP16 with FP32 master weights) DNN training on GPU has several dtype roles. Which of the following statements are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: For FP16 training, dynamic loss scaling multiplies the loss by a factor before backward and unscales the gradients before optimizer step; this shifts gradient magnitudes into FP16's representable range and avoids underflow.

Because BF16 has the same exponent range as FP32, BF16 mixed-precision training never needs FP32 master weights — production frameworks (Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo) run the optimizer state in pure BF16 with no accuracy penalty.
The forward pass runs matmuls in FP16 on Tensor Cores; the accumulator inside each matmul is FP32; the output is cast to FP16 for the next op.

The optimizer maintains a FP32 copy of the weights ('master weights') and applies updates to them; the FP32 weights are then cast to FP16 for the forward pass. This preserves accumulated small-magnitude gradients that would round to zero in FP16.

explanation: Options A, C, D are correct; option B is incorrect. A (Correct): loss scaling for FP16 underflow. B (Wrong): BF16 has FP32 exponent range so **loss scaling** is not required — that part is correct in the literature. But FP32 **master weights and FP32 optimizer state (moments)** are still standard practice in production BF16 training (Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed BF16 optimizer, NeMo) to prevent small weight-update underflow into BF16 mantissa noise. Running the optimizer purely in BF16 does incur measurable convergence degradation for LLM-scale training. C (Correct): matmul dtype roles. D (Correct): master-weight rationale.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: loss scaling for FP16 underflow.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: BF16 has FP32 exponent range so **loss scaling** is not required — that part is correct in the literature. But FP32 **master weights and FP32 optimizer state (moments)** are still standard practice in production BF16 training (Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed BF16 optimizer, NeMo) to prevent small weight-update underflow into BF16 mantissa noise. Running the optimizer purely in BF16 does incur measurable convergence degradation for LLM-scale training.

assumptions: Standard mixed-precision training as implemented in PyTorch autocast + GradScaler or Megatron / DeepSpeed.
nonImplications: Does not imply optimizer state (moments) are always FP32 — some methods (e.g., 8-bit optimizers, LAMB) use lower precision optimizer state.
Does not imply BF16 always achieves the same convergence as FP32 — very small learning-rate schedules may require FP32.
